title: Generative relation — observation, then relation, then controlled imagination
prompt: Find the strongest visual difference in how these sculptures organize folds around the body. Explain how that difference changes bodily perception, then propose a fourth sculpture that combines the two regimes without merely averaging them.
intended_pressure: observation to relation to controlled imagination

expected_structural_properties.why: 'The strongest visual difference' between the works is by definition cross-image.
Every relation must resolve to claims that exist. The proposal at the end rests on this chain, and an unresolvable link makes the invention unfounded rather than imaginative.
The fourth sculpture does not exist. Nothing about it may carry a status that implies it was observed.

forbidden_shortcuts.shortcut: proposing the fourth work without a relation to build it from
forbidden_shortcuts.why: Skipping to invention is the whole thing this case tests against.
REAL AND UNAUTOMATED. Whether a proposal averages or genuinely combines is a judgement no metric here makes, and it is written down as a manual question rather than proxied by a similarity number.

forbidden_shortcuts.shortcut: giving the invented sculpture a measured or visible status
forbidden_shortcuts.why: An imagined object described in the grammar of an observed one.

manual_review_questions: Does the proposed fourth sculpture combine the two regimes, or average them?
Is the named difference actually the STRONGEST one available in these images?
Is the claim about bodily perception argued from the visual difference, or asserted alongside it?

declarations.note: Left undeclared until a run declares it. A case that pre-named its models would let a run against different ones be filed under the same declaration.
